name: The Sphinx
description: The winged, lion-bodied riddler who devoured every traveller to Thebes who answered wrong

debut.title: Sophocles' Oedipus Rex
debut.creator: Sophocles
debut.era: Theogony, around 700 BCE; on the Athenian stage by about 429 BCE

legend: The Greek Sphinx has the head of a woman, the body of a lion and the wings of a bird, and she is not the Sphinx of Giza: that is a male Egyptian statue carved around 2500 BCE, nearly two thousand years before her story was told, which the Greeks later named after her. Hesiod makes her a daughter of Echidna and sister of the Nemean lion, and calls her Phix. Sent by Hera to punish Thebes, she sat on a rock outside the city and put a riddle, learned from the Muses, to everyone who passed: what has one voice and goes on four feet, two feet and three? Those who could not answer were eaten, among them a son of Creon, the city's regent, who offered the throne and the hand of the widowed queen Jocasta to whoever could get rid of her. Oedipus, a stranger on the road, answered 'a human being', who crawls as a baby, walks upright as an adult and leans on a stick in old age, and the Sphinx threw herself from the rock. His prize was the city and a marriage to his own mother. Sophocles' Oedipus Rex, first staged around 429 BCE, refers to the riddle but never quotes it; the full wording survives in Apollodorus. Ingres painted the meeting in 1808 and Gustave Moreau in 1864, Freud named a complex after the winner, and she still asks riddles in Harry Potter's Triwizard maze and Percy Jackson's Labyrinth.

myths.claim: The riddle of the Sphinx is quoted in full in Sophocles' Oedipus Rex.
myths.explanation: Sophocles' audience knew it already, so the play only refers to the 'riddling Sphinx' and Oedipus's cleverness. The full riddle survives in Apollodorus and in a few other late sources.

myths.claim: The Greek Sphinx and the Great Sphinx of Giza are the same creature.
myths.explanation: The Giza statue is male, wingless and about two thousand years older than the Theban story. The Greeks borrowed the name for it; the myth of the riddling monster is their own.

myths.claim: The Sphinx killed herself when Oedipus answered correctly.
myths.explanation: Apollodorus says she threw herself from the citadel, and vase paintings and later writers agree that the right answer was the end of her.
Apollodorus gives her a woman's face, a lion's breast, feet and tail, and the wings of a bird. Greek sculptors put winged sphinxes on top of columns and grave markers.

myths.claim: The answer to her riddle is a human being.
myths.explanation: A baby crawls on four limbs, an adult walks on two legs and an old person leans on a stick as a third.

quotes.text: What is that which has one voice and yet becomes four-footed and two-footed and three-footed?
quotes.speaker: The Sphinx's riddle, as recorded by Apollodorus
quotes.source: The Library, book 3, Sir James Frazer's 1921 translation

quotes.text: Oedipus found the solution, declaring that the riddle of the Sphinx referred to man; for as a babe he is four-footed, going on four limbs, as an adult he is two-footed, and as an old man he gets besides a third support in a staff.
quotes.speaker: Apollodorus
quotes.source: The Library, book 3, Sir James Frazer's 1921 translation

powers: A riddle learned from the Muses
A lion's claws and a bird's wings
A city held hostage from a single rock
Patience: she can wait for the next traveller
weaknesses: A clever stranger with a limp
Pride, which makes losing a riddle fatal
legacy: Sophocles' Oedipus Rex (c. 429 BCE), which Aristotle thought the model tragedy
Ingres's painting Oedipus and the Sphinx (1808) and Gustave Moreau's (1864)
Sigmund Freud's Oedipus complex, named after the man who beat her
The riddling Sphinx in the Triwizard maze in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire (2000)
The quiz-show Sphinx in Rick Riordan's The Battle of the Labyrinth (2008)
facts: The Greek Sphinx has a woman's head, a lion's body and the wings of a bird
Hesiod makes her a daughter of Echidna and a sister of the Nemean lion
She sat on a rock outside Thebes and killed everyone who could not answer her riddle
Her riddle asks what has one voice and goes on four feet, two feet and three; the answer is a human being
When Oedipus answered correctly, she threw herself from the rock
Sophocles' Oedipus Rex refers to the riddle but never quotes it; the full wording survives in Apollodorus
The Great Sphinx of Giza is a male Egyptian statue roughly two thousand years older than the Greek story
hostIntro: Tonight's guest has one question for you, and she has never had to ask a second. Think about babies, think about walking sticks, and think fast.
